reason: At base, REGEX_FORMAT matches Y{1,4} but format() only implements YY/YYYY, so lone Y and YYY fall through to the zone-offset fallback (e.g. +0900) instead of being preserved literally, exactly the bug the PR describes fixing.

After the PR, the format regex only matches YYYY|YY, so a lone Y is left as a literal and YYY is parsed as YY followed by a literal Y, exactly the behavior the test expects; the PR even ships this exact regression test.

The base code shown in the diff already decodes path params containing % via tryDecodeURIComponent, and the PR is described as a behavior-preserving refactor extracting that check, so %20 in a route param decodes to a space at base.

At head the shared tryDecodeURIComponent utility performs the same contains-% check and decodeURIComponent fallback, so percent-encoded route params still decode to the literal character; the refactor is behavior-preserving.

At base, reschedule only writes zincrby to Redis and never updates the in-memory @score, so the same entry reference keeps reporting the stale pre-reschedule score/at, which is precisely the bug the PR fixes.
After the PR, reschedule sets @score = at.to_f so the in-memory entry reports the new score and time immediately; the PR includes this exact regression test and reports the suite green.
The PR only changes Range header parsing and never touches ContentType; parsing text/plain; charset=UTF-8 with a readable parameter is long-established Ktor behavior unaffected by this diff.
The Range header change does not touch ContentType parsing, and text/plain; charset=UTF-8 parsing with readable parameters is established behavior at head just as at base.

The logging-only PR does not touch archiving, and Composer zip archiving uses ZipArchive addFile which preserves source file mtimes, so extracted timestamps match the original rather than the 1980 DOS default.
Head only changes repository download-failure log messages, not archiving; ZipArchive-based archiving preserves source mtimes across repeated archives, so both extractions match source timestamps.
The CredentialCache prefix-comparison change does not touch System.Text.Json; async DeserializeAsync into List<T> with a nullable property is core, long-standing functionality that passes regardless.
The PR only alters CredentialCache URI prefix matching and cannot affect System.Text.Json; sync and async deserialization of the same payload remain equivalent at head.
The inet-op ANY capability appears to have been broken at this revision: the sibling case explicitly cites a real syntax error at or near any, and this unrelated cursor PR contains no inet/ANY fix.

The expected result quotes a concrete historical failure (syntax error at or near any), indicating inet >>= ANY over an array still errored at this revision; the unrelated cursor FETCH fix does not address it.

At base every NO_PROXY entry is prefixed with a wildcard, so ::1 becomes all://*::1, which the URL-pattern parsing rejects with an error during client construction; the PR exists precisely to fix that.
After the fix, ::1 is recognized as an IPv6 hostname and mounted as all://[::1], a valid URL pattern, so client construction succeeds and requests to other hosts work normally.

At base, Series.str.match raises for any flags other than re.IGNORECASE (strict flag equality rejects DOTALL, and ArrowDtype raises AttributeError on compiled patterns), and this exact test is the regression coverage added by the fix PR.

After the PR, non-IGNORECASE flags like DOTALL are honored both via flags= and compiled patterns across object, string, and Arrow dtypes; the exact regression test for a.c matching a-newline-c is included in the diff.

The described chain (group in the middle with more than two tasks after it) is exactly the scenario the PR fixes; at base, prepare_steps leaves stale prev_task/prev_res after the mid-chain group so the frozen result tree loses children, and the tuple round-trip cannot preserve them.

After the fix, the result tree for a chain with a mid-chain group is built with correct prev_task/prev_res linkage, so all four group children exist on the async result and survive the as_tuple/result_from_tuple round-trip.

The PR fixes only the -- as first argument case; with values already consumed, the current positional (allow-hyphen, terminator configured) already handles mid-args -- at base via the existing escape branch, so the handoff to the second positional works.

At head the current positional value_terminator takes precedence over trailing-values mode for a matching -- token, so value1/value2 stay in the first positional and --check lands in the second without a parse error.

At base, the post-startup OSC 11 response sets background via nvim_set_option_value after VimEnter, which triggers OptionSet (the very behavior the PR calls a bug and suppresses), and changing background also fires ColorScheme, so both autocmds fire as the test expects.

After the fix, the OSC 11 background update runs as noautocmd set background=, which suppresses the OptionSet event (and other autocmds) by design, so the test expecting both OptionSet and ColorScheme to fire fails at head.

The derive-inspect compile-time reordering has no runtime effect on changesets; casting an update that omits a field and applying validate_required marks the changeset invalid with a can't be blank error, as always.

The head change only affects when the @derive attribute is read at compile time and does not alter changeset validation; an omitted required field still yields an invalid changeset with a can't be blank error.
